"Before I formed you in the womb I knew you." What does it mean that God knew you before you were born?
Jeremiah said, "I am only a youth," and God said, "Do not be afraid... for I am with you." What excuse do you give God?
God put his words in Jeremiah's mouth. How does God equip those he calls?
"They will fight against you, but they shall not prevail, for I am with you." Where do you need this promise?
God remembered Israel's early devotion. How is your first love for God?
God's people forsook "the fountain of living waters" for broken cisterns. What broken cisterns do people dig today?
"Can a virgin forget her ornaments...? Yet my people have forgotten me days without number." What causes us to forget God?
"Return, faithless Israel... for I am merciful." What does God's call to return show about him?
"I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding." How can you pray for your church's shepherds?
"Return, O faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness." Where do you need God's healing?
"If you return, O Israel... to me you should return." What would returning wholeheartedly look like?
"Break up your fallow ground." What hard ground in your heart needs breaking up?
Jeremiah felt anguish over his people. What breaks your heart for others?
God asked them to search for one person who does justice and seeks truth. How can you be that person?
People had eyes but did not see. What might you be blind to?
"They have healed the wound of my people lightly, saying, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace." How can we avoid shallow comfort?
"Stand by the roads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls." What are the ancient paths for you?
The people trusted the temple instead of changing their ways. What religious habits might we trust instead of God?
"Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people." What does this relationship mean?
Even birds know their seasons, but God's people did not know his ways. How can you be attentive to God?
"Is there no balm in Gilead?" Where do you see wounds that need God's healing?
Jeremiah wished his eyes were a fountain of tears for his people. What grieves your heart?
"Let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me." What do you boast in?
"There is none like you, O Lord; you are great." What makes God incomparable?
"The Lord is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King." How does this shape your trust?
"It is not in man who walks to direct his steps." How do you seek God's direction?
God reminded them of his covenant. How does God's covenant shape your relationship with him?
Jeremiah committed his cause to God when plotted against. How do you handle opposition?
Jeremiah asked, "Why does the way of the wicked prosper?" How do you bring such questions to God?
"If you have raced with men on foot, and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses?" How does God prepare you for harder things?
God promised compassion even to the nations if they learned his ways. What does this show about God's mercy?
The ruined loincloth showed how pride ruins people. How can pride spoil us?
God wanted his people to cling to him "for a name, a praise, and a glory." What does clinging to God look like?
"Can the leopard change his spots?" What does this show about our need for God to change us?
"Though our iniquities testify against us, act, O Lord, for your name's sake." How does this prayer shape yours?
"We set our hope on you, for you do all these things." Where is your hope set?
Jeremiah felt his pain was unending. How can you bring raw honesty to God?
"Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart." How do you take in God's word?
God told Jeremiah, "If you return, I will restore you." What does God's restoring mean?
God would bring them back from the north as he did from Egypt. What new acts of rescue has God done for you?
"O Lord, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble." How has God been your refuge?
"Cursed is the man who trusts in man... whose heart turns away from the Lord." Where might you trust people more than God?
"Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord... He is like a tree planted by water." What does that tree picture mean to you?
"The heart is deceitful above all things." How can you let God search your heart?
"Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed." Where do you need God's healing?
"Like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand." How do you let God shape you?
God relents when people turn from evil. What does this show about his mercy?
The people filled the place with the blood of innocents. What does this show about how far people can turn from God?
The broken flask showed coming judgement. What does this teach about the seriousness of sin?
Jeremiah said God's word was like a burning fire shut up in his bones. What compels you to speak of God?
"The Lord is with me as a dread warrior." How does God's presence give you courage?
"Sing to the Lord; praise the Lord!" How can you praise God even when things are hard?
"I set before you the way of life and the way of death." What choices are before you?
"Execute justice in the morning, and deliver from the hand of the oppressor him who has been robbed." How can you act justly?
"Do justice and righteousness... do no wrong or violence to the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow." Who needs your protection?
"He judged the cause of the poor and needy... Is not this to know me?" How does caring for the poor relate to knowing God?
God says, "Woe to the shepherds who scatter the sheep." How does God care for his flock?
God will raise a righteous Branch called "The Lord is our righteousness." How does this point to Jesus?
"Do I not fill heaven and earth?" What does God's presence everywhere mean to you?
"Is not my word like fire... and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?" How has God's word worked in you?
God saw the exiles as good figs he would care for. How does God see people the world may overlook?
God says, "I will give them a heart to know that I am the Lord." What does this new heart mean to you?
Jeremiah spoke persistently for twenty-three years, but they did not listen. How do you keep going when no one listens?
God set the exile at seventy years. What does this show about God's control over history?
God said, "Do not hold back a word. It may be they will listen." How can you speak God's truth faithfully?
Jeremiah stood firm though his life was threatened. What does courage in speaking truth look like?
"It is I who by my great power... have made the earth." How does God's power shape your view of the world?
Jeremiah urged the king not to listen to prophets who were lying. How can you tell true from false comfort?
Jeremiah wished Hananiah's hopeful prophecy were true, but tested it against God's word. How do you test what you hear?
Hananiah made people trust in a lie. Why is false comfort dangerous?
God told the exiles to build houses and seek the welfare of the city. How can you seek the good of your city?
"I know the plans I have for you... plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope." How does this promise encourage you?
"You will seek me and find me, when you seek me with all your heart." What does seeking God wholeheartedly look like?
"Fear not, O Jacob my servant... for I am with you to save you." What fear do you need to bring to God?
"I will restore health to you, and your wounds I will heal." Where do you need healing?
"You shall be my people, and I will be your God." What does this relationship mean to you?
"I have loved you with an everlasting love." What does God's everlasting love mean to you?
"I will turn their mourning into joy." When has God done this for you?
"I will satisfy the weary soul." Where are you weary?
God promises a new covenant: "I will put my law within them... I will forgive their iniquity." How does Jesus bring this new covenant?
Jeremiah bought a field during the siege as a sign of hope. How can you act in hope when things look bleak?
"Ah, Lord God! It is you who have made the heavens and the earth... Nothing is too hard for you." What seems too hard for you?
God promises one heart and one way so that they may fear him forever. What does God want to do in your heart?
"Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things." What would you ask God?
"I will bring to it health and healing... and reveal to them abundance of prosperity and security." What healing do you long for?
God will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David. How does this point to Jesus?
The people freed their slaves but then took them back. Why is it important to keep our promises?
God said they had not proclaimed liberty. What does true freedom for others look like?
The Rechabites faithfully obeyed their father's command. What does their faithfulness teach you?
God contrasts their obedience with Israel's disobedience. Where do you need to listen to God more?
God hoped the people would hear and turn. What does this show about God's heart?
The king cut up and burned the scroll. How do people reject God's word today?
God had Jeremiah write the words again. What does this show about God's word lasting?
Neither the king nor the people listened to God's words. What keeps us from listening?
The king secretly asked Jeremiah, "Is there any word from the Lord?" Why might people seek God's word in secret?
Jeremiah was thrown into a muddy cistern for speaking truth. What has faithfulness cost you?
Ebed-melech rescued Jeremiah. How can you stand up for someone being mistreated?
Jerusalem fell just as God had said. What does this show about taking God's warnings seriously?
God promised to deliver Ebed-melech "because you have put your trust in me." How does God honour trust?
Jeremiah was set free and chose to stay with the poor in the land. What does his choice teach you?
The scattered people gathered and began to harvest again. How does God bring new beginnings after loss?
Ishmael committed treachery and murder. How does violence spread when people reject God?
Johanan rescued the captives but still feared. How does fear shape our decisions?
The people asked Jeremiah to pray and promised to obey whatever God said. How sincere are your promises to God?
God said, "Do not fear the king of Babylon... for I am with you." What fear do you need to face with God?
The people called God's word a lie when it didn't suit them. How do you respond when God's word is not what you want?
Even in Egypt, God's word followed them. What does this show about running from God?
The people insisted on worshipping the queen of heaven. Why do people cling to false worship?
"They shall know whose word will stand, mine or theirs." How does God's word prove true?
God told Baruch, "Do you seek great things for yourself? Seek them not." What great things might you be seeking?
God promised Baruch his life wherever he went. What does it mean that God keeps you?
Egypt's pride was brought low. What does this show about trusting in human power?
"Fear not, O Jacob my servant... for I am with you." What does God's presence mean in uncertain times?
Judgement came on the Philistines. What does this show about God ruling over all nations?
The sword of the Lord would not be quiet until his purpose was done. What does this show about God's purposes?
Moab had been at ease and settled. What dangers come with comfort?
Moab's pride and arrogance were judged. How does God see pride?
Yet God says he will restore the fortunes of Moab. What does this show about God's mercy?
God promises to restore the fortunes of the Ammonites. What does this show about God's heart for the nations?
"Leave your fatherless children; I will keep them alive; and let your widows trust in me." How does God care for the vulnerable?
The people will come weeping and seeking the Lord, joining him in an everlasting covenant. What does returning to God look like?
"My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray." How does Jesus seek lost sheep?
God says the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there shall be none, for he will pardon. What does God's pardon mean to you?
"Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name." How does God's strength as Redeemer comfort you?
God made the earth by his power and wisdom. What does creation show you about God?
"Let not your heart faint, and be not fearful at the report heard in the land." How do you stay steady with bad news?
Jerusalem fell as God had warned. What does this show about God's word?
Jehoiachin was released and given a seat at the king's table. What hope does this ending give?
